title: fix(metadata-protocol): seed reference probe names the repair a republish reaches, judged once per object
body:

## 维护者速读

- 发布后检查示例数据时，若示例记录指向不存在的记录，构建回执现在会按示例数据的写入方式给出真正有效的修复办法；同一对象有多份示例数据时只报一次。
- 属于发布后构建检查这条线，替按默认方式（不覆盖已有记录）发布示例数据的作者和 AI 解决"照提示修了却没生效、回执却变干净"的问题。
- 只影响发布回执里的警告文字和判断范围，不拦截发布、不改数据；出错最多是提示措辞不准，可直接撤回。
- 无

## What changes

`seed_reference_unresolved` (build probe, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts`):

- **Judged per object, not per seed.** `seedApplied.landed` is one entry per object for every seed of it (`seedAppliedLanded`), so the probe now groups the published seeds by object and emits one finding per object and reference column. The finding's `artifact` is the object's first published seed; `message` names every seed of the object.
- **Which landed rows are judged.** Rows the publish created (`landed.inserted`): always. Rows a seed key matched (`landed.matched`): only when every published seed of the object declares `upsert` or `update`, and only in a column every one of those seeds writes back onto a matched row: every record carries the column and the seed does not declare `columns.FIELD.applyOn: 'create'` (key fields excepted, as the loader does). Any other column of a matched row is its writer's and is not judged.
- **The repair named is the one a republish reaches** (`fix`, and a new `cause` param on the `userMessage`, all 11 locales):
  - `seed`: every seed rewrites the column on a matched row, so correcting the seed and republishing works.
  - `mixed`: some seeds of the object write the column back onto a matched row and some do not, and the receipt cannot tell which seed landed which row: correct the value in every seed, then correct, clear or delete the rows the other seeds leave as they are (or declare `upsert` on them where that alone reaches the column); `fix` names the writing seeds and the others by reason.
  - `mode`: every seed of the object is `ignore`, and declaring `upsert` would make the replay write the column: correct, clear or delete the stored rows, or declare `mode: 'upsert'` and correct the seed.
  - `stored`: no mode change makes the seed write the column on a row it finds again (`applyOn: 'create'`, or a record that does not carry the column): correct, clear or delete the stored rows; `fix` names which seed has which reason.
  - The `mixed`, `mode` and `stored` `fix` texts end by saying that until a repair is done the next receipt carries no finding for those rows (a republish that changes nothing reads clean).

`rollup_never_computed` nits: the `message` says "of one organization" only when the pass was split by organization, which needs the child object to carry a tenant column (an object with no tenant column is one unscoped pass, also when the publish names an organization), and says "sampled parent row(s)"; the `userMessage` in all 11 locales says "the records checked" instead of "every record"; the unreleased changeset's "every parent" is corrected. The organization discovery's 50-row sample keeps its shape and its reason is now stated on `probeOrganizations`: the list is a loop bound (two reads per organization on the publish request), and a distinct read pushed down would return every organization of the table.

One new changeset (`patch`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`). No new finding code, no new catalog key, no new export.

## Why

Under the default `mode: 'ignore'` a republish leaves a row it finds again as it is (`seed-loader.ts` `writeRecord`, the `ignore` arm returns `skipped` with the existing id). So the old repair, "correct the seed and republish", changed nothing, and the next receipt came back clean because the probe did not read matched rows under `ignore`. And with two seeds of one object, a row only an `ignore` seed matched was judged under the other seed's mode, and each seed reported the same value again.

New cases, in the shared landed-data harness (`build-probes-landed-data.test.ts`, a new top-level `describe`, per AGENTS.md's shared-harness rule) and as `CASES` rows of `build-probes-user-message.test.ts` (one per `cause`, four values, each rendered in all 11 locales):

- under `ignore`: the first publish's finding names the stored-row or `upsert` repair (`cause: 'mode'`); a republish under `ignore` (row now matched) is not the seed's to judge; after declaring `upsert` the matched row keeps being reported with the seed repair until it resolves, then goes silent;
- one `ignore` and one `upsert` seed of one object: exactly one finding, over the created row only (the matched row's value is not quoted), with the `mixed` repair naming the `upsert` seed as writing the column back;
- two `upsert` seeds of one object: their matched rows in one finding;
- `applyOn: 'create'` and a record without the column: the matched row's column is not judged; the created row is, with the stored-row repair;
- `rollup_never_computed` on an object with no tenant column: the message claims no organization, also when the publish names an organization.

<details><summary>Ablations (one-off, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to HEAD blob each time)</summary>

The tests import `./build-probes.js` from `src`, so no `dist` rebuild is in the path.

1. `seeds.every(` to `seeds.some(` for the writing-mode test: the mixed-seeds case goes red (1 failed / 25).
2. `rewritten = writing` (drop the per-column rewrite check): the column-not-written case and the `stored` user-message case go red (2 failed / 73).
3. `cause` `mode` branch replaced by `false`: the `ignore` case, the mixed case and the `mode` user-message case go red (3 failed / 73).
4. The "of one organization" condition forced on: the unscoped roll-up case goes red (1 failed / 26). The first attempt at this one was a no-op (the replacement text already occurred in the file and the tool refused); it was re-run with a distinct replacement.

Every leg ended `ok restored: blob == HEAD` with `git diff HEAD` empty.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Done-when 1 is met through the repair text. Under `ignore` a republish never writes a matched row, and the binding scope reads matched rows only when every seed writes, so a republish under `ignore` with nothing else changed still comes back clean. What changed is the first receipt: its repair is one that works (fix or delete the stored rows, or declare `upsert`). After `upsert` the row keeps being reported until it resolves (pinned).
- Done-when 2: rows the publish created count as written by a seed, whatever its mode (an insert is a write under `ignore` too). A matched row is judged only when every seed of the object writes.
- Per-row precision: the probe cannot tell which record a landed id came from, so "the seed writes this column on a matched row" needs every record of every seed of the object to carry it. A seed where only some records carry a column gets the stored-row repair for that column, which is conservative but always works.
- Overlap check: the only overlap is the standing Version Packages PR, which deletes every unreleased changeset, including the one this PR corrects. That conflict is expected for any edit to an unreleased changeset, and that PR is regenerated from `main`.

## Verification

- Read first, by risk: `build-probes.ts` (the seed-reference section, where the rows judged are chosen per column, and the `seedRewritesOnMatch` helpers), then `build-probes.user-text.ts` (the `SEED_REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED` entry).
- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run src/build-probes-landed-data.test.ts`. Expect 26 passed, including the new `seed_reference_unresolved is judged per object` block.

### DELIBERATE CORRECTION

`.changeset/34776-publish-checks-build-probes.md` is an unreleased note this PR corrects, because the behaviour it describes changed here. One sentence changed. Before: "`rollup_never_computed` (a roll-up blank on every parent that has children)". After: "`rollup_never_computed` (a roll-up blank on all of the sampled parents that have children, judged inside one organization when the rows carry one)". `check-empty-changeset` stays red on it, as it should.
